pr_body:
Motivation:

If DeleteOnExitHook is in the open state and the program runs for a long time, the DeleteOnExitHook file keeps increasing.
This results in a cause memory leak

![10351](https://github.com/wuxiansen/question-library/blob/master/netty/10351.png) 

See https://github.com/netty/netty/issues/10351

Modification:

I re-customized a DeleteOnExitHook hook. If DeleteOnExitHook is turned on, this hook will be added when creating a temporary file. After the request ends and the corresponding resources are released, the current file will be removed from this hook, so that it will not increase all the time.

Result:

Fixes #[10351](https://github.com/netty/netty/issues/10351).

comments: `4.1.15.Final` was released around 3 years ago and Netty received numerous updates till now, Can you check if this issue happens with `4.1.50.Final` too?

review_comments: We should also have a test that verifies that the registered files are deleted by the shut down hook.
If the file does not exist, return false .
security manager still might throw an exception or NPE if null was passed as path.
`ConcurrentHashMap` key not be null.  so avoided this problem

Tests don't run in any particular order, so this test also needs to do the work to ensure that some file uploads are created. It can then call `runHooks` directly (since it has package visibility) to simulate the shutdown.
With a Set based on ConcurrentHashMap, we can just iterate it directly. Since we are at JVM shut down at this point, I don't think we need to clear the set.
